# Contributing to hypersuite

hypersuite helps people take their data back: clean up a Windows machine,
leave the Outlook realm, and get their files and mail into a state that is
ready for a move to Linux. Development happens on a self-hosted, independent
Git server; the source code is not published, to keep it out of large-scale
AI training pipelines and to keep the project's direction in our hands.

Bug reports, ideas and questions are always welcome — use the
[issue forms](https://github.com/namshubs/hypersuite/issues/new/choose) or
[Discussions](https://github.com/namshubs/hypersuite/discussions). No access
needed for that.

## Access to the source code

We work on hypersuite in our spare time, so we keep the circle of
contributors small and the onboarding thorough. Access is given to people
who meet **all** of the following:

1. **You are a human.** Contributions come from people, not from AI agents
   or bots. The onboarding includes a live conversation.
2. **No ties to Big Tech.** You don't work for, contract for or represent the
   large platform companies whose products hypersuite helps people leave.
   The easiest way to show this is a link to your LinkedIn (or similar)
   profile; your involvement in similar projects, or the interview, works as
   well.
3. **You stand for user rights.** You have contributed to privacy-related
   projects, or written or spoken for the rights of users against Big Tech —
   please link to it.
4. **You have a technical improvement agenda.** You know what you want to
   improve in hypersuite (a feature, a fix, performance, Linux support,
   documentation) and roughly how.

## How it works

1. Open a Discussion in the **Contributor access** category, or an issue
   with the [Contributor access](https://github.com/namshubs/hypersuite/issues/new?template=contributor_access.yml)
   form, and cover the four points above.
2. If it looks like a fit, we arrange an interactive onboarding: a
   conversation about you, your agenda and how we work.
3. You sign the [contributor agreement](CONTRIBUTOR-AGREEMENT.md): you keep
   the copyright in your work and license it to the project, you keep the
   source code confidential, and we keep hypersuite free for its users.
4. Then you get an invitation to the development server.

We may not answer every request, and a "no" is not a judgement of you. If
we don't see a fit, we say so early rather than waste your time — or ours.
